newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened little changed in very quiet trade on Tuesday as a lack of significant economic data helped to keep flows light, analysts said.

"The U.S. is quiet and we're quiet. The only thing that traders can focus on this week is the auctions," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "To me the market is just going sideways right now. We don't get any real big numbers until next week."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.02 to C$108.25 to yield 7.288 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 7.09 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 20 basis points from 19 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

Canadian economic reports on retail sales and the consumer price index report for March had almost no impact on the Canadian market this morning, Dong said. Instead, bonds investors remain focused on U.S. economic data out next week.

In the interim bond investors are paying closest attention to bond auctions in both Canada and the United States. The Government of Canada tomorrow will auction C$1.3 billion of 30-year bonds, all of it new cash.
"With our 30-year bond auction tomorrow, it looks to me like there is probably going be decent demand for that issue, just judging by the way it's been trading for the last few days," said Dong.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.03 to C$101.82 to yield 6.738 percent. The U.S. bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 13 basis points from 14 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.19 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.34 percent.
